tables.description: Comparative analysis of lighting effects on human well-being and performance from different studies, including study objectives, methodology, and major findings related to lighting.

limitations: Small sample sizes and limited to single groups in several studies (Cupkova et al. [4], Kim et al. [12], Kazemi et al. [11], Sun et al. [20]).
Difficulty generalizing results beyond specific populations (e.g., postgraduate students, young college students) [11, 12, 20].
Privacy concerns with data collection methods (e.g., Digital ID in Deng et al. [5]).
Limitations in experimental techniques and model approaches in some studies [14, 10].
Failure to account for temporal variables (e.g., morning vs. afternoon) affecting working memory [14].
Lack of clear distinction between sunlight and artificial light during illuminance measurements [10].
Insufficient deep research on the impact of lighting glare and Colour Rendering Index (CRI) on human behaviour, visual performance, and comfort.
